questions.q: Definite IE on Book p69 is diagnosed by the pathological criteria, or 2 major + ____, or 1 major + ____, or ____ minor.
questions.exp: Book p69 IE diagnosis, definitive: i. pathological criteria; ii. 2 major + 1 minor; iii. 1 major + 2 minor; iv. 5 minor. (Book p69)

questions.q: Possible IE on Book p69 is:
questions.exp: Book p69 IE diagnosis b: 'possible : 1 major + 1 minor or 3 minor'. (Book p69)

questions.q: All of the following are combinations for DEFINITE IE on Book p69 EXCEPT:
questions.exp: Definite IE (Book p69): pathological criteria, 2 major + 1 minor, 1 major + 2 minor, or 5 minor. '1 major + 1 minor' is only the first possible-IE combination (alongside 3 minor). (Book p69)

questions.q: Match the four blood-culture major-criteria entries on Book p69 to their detail — 1) Typical organisms from two blood cultures 2) The 'or' entry within typical organisms 3) Other organisms from persistently positive cultures 4) Single positive culture / serology … A) Viridans streptococci, Streptococcus bovis, HACEK group (Haemophilus, Actinobacillus, Cardiobacterium, Eikenella, Kingella) B) Community-acquired Staphylococcus aureus or enterococci in the absence of a primary focus C) Two positive cultures of samples drawn >12 hours apart, or all of three or a majority of four separate cultures (first and last sample drawn 1 hour apart) D) Single positive culture for Coxiella burnetii, or positive serology for Q fever, Bartonella species and Chlamydia psittaci
questions.exp: Book p69 major criteria, blood cultures positive: typical microorganisms from two blood cultures (Viridans streptococci, Streptococcus bovis, HACEK group — Haemophilus, Actinobacillus, Cardiobacterium, Eikenella, Kingella), OR community-acquired S. aureus or enterococci without a primary focus; OR other organisms from persistently positive cultures (two positive cultures >12 h apart, or all of three / majority of four, first and last 1 h apart); OR single positive culture for Coxiella burnetii or positive serology for Q fever, Bartonella species and Chlamydia psittaci. (Book p69)

questions.q: The HACEK group in the Book p69 major criteria comprises ____, ____, ____, ____ and ____.
questions.exp: Book p69: HACEK group = (Haemophilus, Actinobacillus, Cardiobacterium, Eikenella, Kingella). (Book p69)

questions.q: A patient grows an organism that is not on the typical list, in cultures from draws 14 hours apart. Per the Book p69 major criteria, what defines 'persistently positive' blood cultures for other microorganisms?
opts: A single positive culture from any draw
Two positive cultures drawn within 6 hours of each other
Two positive cultures of blood samples drawn >12 hours apart, or all of three or a majority of four separate cultures with the first and last sample drawn 1 hour apart
One positive culture from two separate venipunctures on the same day
questions.exp: Book p69: other microorganisms consistent with IE from persistently positive blood cultures defined as — two positive cultures of blood samples drawn >12 hours apart, or all of three or a majority of four separate cultures of blood (with first and last sample drawn 1 hour apart). (Book p69)

questions.q: Match the four echocardiographic entries that make the echo 'positive for IE' on Book p69 to their detail — 1) Oscillating mass 2) Abscess 3) Prosthetic valve 4) Valvular regurgitation … A) Oscillating intracardiac mass without alternative explanation B) The second listed echocardiographic entry C) New partial dehiscence of prosthetic valve D) New valvular regurgitation (worsening or changing of preexisting murmur not sufficient)
questions.exp: Book p69 major criteria: evidence of endocardial involvement — echocardiogram positive for IE: oscillating intracardiac mass without alternative explanation, or abscess, or new partial dehiscence of prosthetic valve, or new valvular regurgitation (worsening or changing of preexisting murmur not sufficient). (Book p69)

questions.q: Per the Book p69 major criteria, why is a 'worsening or changing of preexisting murmur' explicitly not sufficient?
opts: Murmur changes cannot be recorded on echocardiography
Only a NEW valvular regurgitation satisfies the echocardiographic major criterion
It implies the murmur is rheumatic in origin
A preexisting murmur excludes infective endocarditis
questions.exp: Book p69: the echocardiographic entry requires NEW valvular regurgitation — 'worsening or changing of preexisting murmur not sufficient'. (Book p69)

questions.q: A positive echocardiogram for IE on Book p69 shows an oscillating intracardiac mass without alternative explanation, or ____, or a new partial dehiscence of prosthetic valve, or ____.
opts: new valvular stenosis; new atrial septal defect
questions.exp: Book p69 echo entries: oscillating intracardiac mass without alternative explanation, or abscess, or new partial dehiscence of prosthetic valve, or new valvular regurgitation. (Book p69)

questions.q: Match the four minor-criteria bullets on Book p69 to their content — 1) Predisposition 2) Fever 3) Vascular phenomena 4) Immunologic phenomena … A) Predisposing heart condition, injection drug use, previous infective endocarditis, or prosthetic valve or material B) Temperature >38°C C) Major arterial emboli, septic pulmonary infarcts, mycotic aneurysm, intracranial haemorrhages, subconjunctival petechiae, Janeway lesions D) Glomerulonephritis, Osler's nodes, Roth's spots, positive rheumatoid factor
questions.exp: Book p69 minor criteria: predisposition (heart condition, injection drug use, previous IE, prosthetic valve or material); fever >38°C; vascular phenomena (major arterial emboli, septic pulmonary infarcts, mycotic aneurysm, intracranial haemorrhages, subconjunctival petechiae, Janeway lesions); immunologic phenomena (glomerulonephritis, Osler's nodes, Roth's spots, positive rheumatoid factor). (Book p69)

questions.q: Match the five physical findings on Book p69 to the minor-criteria list they belong to — 1) Janeway lesions 2) Osler's nodes 3) Roth's spots 4) Subconjunctival petechiae 5) Glomerulonephritis … A) Vascular phenomena list B) Immunologic phenomena list C) Immunologic phenomena list D) Vascular phenomena list E) Immunologic phenomena list
questions.exp: Book p69: vascular phenomena include major arterial emboli, septic pulmonary infarcts, mycotic aneurysm, intracranial haemorrhages, subconjunctival petechiae and Janeway lesions; immunologic phenomena include glomerulonephritis, Osler's nodes, Roth's spots and positive rheumatoid factor. (Book p69)

questions.q: The 'microbiological evidence' minor criterion on Book p69: a positive blood culture that does not meet a major criterion, or ____ evidence of active infection with organisms consistent with infective endocarditis.
questions.exp: Book p69 minor criteria: 'Microbiological evidence: Positive blood culture but does not meet a major criterion or serological evidence of active infection with organisms consistent with infective endocarditis'. (Book p69)

questions.q: The pathological criterion on Book p69 is:
opts: Two positive blood cultures from separate venipunctures
Positive microbiology or histology of pathologic tissue material attained at surgery or autopsy (vegetations, valve tissue, embolic fragments or tissue/pus from intracardiac abscesses)
A vegetation seen only on cardiac CT
questions.exp: Book p69: 'Pathological criteria — Positive microbiology or histology of pathologic tissue material attained at surgery or autopsy (vegetations, valve tissue, embolic fragments or tissue/pus from intracardiac abscesses)'. (Book p69)

questions.q: Match the four cells of the 'for oral procedures' prophylaxis table on Book p70 to its regimen — 1) Can take oral (no allergy) 2) Cannot take oral (no allergy) 3) Can take oral + penicillin allergy 4) Cannot take oral + penicillin allergy … A) Amoxicillin B) Ampicillin ; ceftriaxone C) Clindamycin ; azithro D) Clindamycin ; ceftriaxone
questions.exp: Book p70 oral-procedures table: penicillin row — can take oral: amoxicillin; cannot take oral: ampicillin; ceftriaxone. Penicillin-allergy row — can take oral: clindamycin; azithro; cannot take oral: clindamycin; ceftriaxone. (Book p70)

questions.q: For RESP procedure prophylaxis on Book p70, abscess/empyema drainage requires adding coverage for ____, and staph is covered with ____.
questions.exp: Book p70 prophylaxis — RESP: i. same as oral; ii. abscess/empyema drainage include below; iii. strep viridans; iv. staph : Vanco. (Book p70)

questions.q: Which of the following True/False statements correctly reflects the old prophylaxis page (Book p70)?
opts: True: GU or GIT prophylaxis is not recommended, but in patients with established infection or under antibiotic cover, enterococci are covered with penicillin
False: SSTI prophylaxis is not recommended for routine surgery
True: clindamycin; azithro is the first-line non-allergic oral regimen
False: if SSTI surgery involves infected skin or musculoskeletal tissue and the patient is allergic or MRSA, Vance is used
questions.exp: Book p70: GU or GIT — not recommended; pts with established infx or under abx cover to prevent sepsis during procedure: enterococci — penicillin. SSTI — not recommended for routine sx; if sx involves infected skin or musculoskeletal: anti strep or staph — penicillin; if allergic or MRSA — Vance. (Book p70)

questions.q: The highlighted note at the foot of Book p70 states:
opts: The 2023 ESC guideline and 2023 Duke-ISCVID criteria have superseded the above — see the UPDATE pages that follow, including prophylaxis
The 2023 Duke-ISCVID criteria replace only the diagnosis table, not prophylaxis
The p70 prophylaxis regimens remain current for RESP procedures
The 2015 ESC guidelines supersede this page
questions.exp: Book p70, foot note: '* IE — 2023 ESC guideline and 2023 Duke-ISCVID criteria have superseded the above. See the UPDATE pages that follow, including prophylaxis.' (Book p70)

questions.q: Which of the following True/False statements correctly reflects what Duke-ISCVID changed (Book p71)?
opts: False: the separate-venipuncture / defined-time-interval blood-culture requirement has been removed
True: definite IE is unchanged in structure — 2 major, or 1 major + 3 minor, or 5 minor
True: cardiac CT and 18F-FDG PET/CT became major imaging criteria only for prosthetic valves
False: previous IE is now a predisposing condition
questions.exp: Book p71: definite IE unchanged in structure — 2 major, or 1 major + 3 minor, or 5 minor; possible IE 1 major + 1 minor, or 3 minor. Cardiac CT and 18F-FDG PET/CT are now major imaging criteria — no longer restricted to prosthetic valves; intraoperative inspection by the surgeon is a NEW major clinical criterion. (Book p71)

questions.q: Match the six Duke-ISCVID changes on Book p71 to their detail — 1) Blood-culture rules 2) Typical organism list 3) New microbiological methods 4) Imaging major criteria 5) Intraoperative inspection 6) New minor criteria … A) Relaxed — the separate-venipuncture / defined-time-interval requirement has been removed B) Expanded, with a second tier that counts as typical only if intracardiac prosthetic material is present (e.g. coagulase-negative staphylococci, Cutibacterium acnes, corynebacteria) C) PCR, amplicon and metagenomic sequencing, in-situ hybridisation, and enzyme immunoassay for Bartonella D) Cardiac CT and 18F-FDG PET/CT are now major imaging criteria — no longer restricted to prosthetic valves E) A new major clinical criterion by the surgeon F) Previous IE is now a predisposing condition; predisposing lesions broadened (transcatheter valves, CIEDs)
questions.exp: Book p71 'DIAGNOSIS — WHAT DUKE-ISCVID CHANGED': blood-culture rules relaxed (separate venipunctures at defined time intervals removed); typical organism list expanded with a prosthetic-material second tier; new microbiological methods (PCR, amplicon/metagenomic sequencing, in-situ hybridisation, enzyme immunoassay for Bartonella); imaging majors widened (cardiac CT, 18F-FDG PET/CT, no longer prosthetic-valve-only); intraoperative inspection a new major clinical criterion; new minors (previous IE a predisposing condition; transcatheter valves, CIEDs added). (Book p71)

questions.q: Which organisms count as typical ONLY if intracardiac prosthetic material is present (the Duke-ISCVID second tier, Book p71)?
questions.exp: Book p71: a second tier was added of organisms that count as typical only if intracardiac prosthetic material is present (e.g. coagulase-negative staphylococci, Cutibacterium acnes, corynebacteria). (Book p71)

questions.q: The new microbiological methods accepted by Duke-ISCVID (Book p71): ____, ____ and metagenomic sequencing, in-situ hybridisation, and enzyme immunoassay for ____.
questions.exp: Book p71: 'New microbiological methods accepted: PCR, amplicon and metagenomic sequencing, in-situ hybridisation, and enzyme immunoassay for Bartonella.' (Book p71)

questions.q: Match the six rows of the management-by-type table in the 'FIVE BUCKETS' section (Book p71) to their regimen — 1) Native valve, community-acquired 2) Prosthetic valve, EARLY (<12 months) 3) Prosthetic valve, LATE (>12 months) 4) Right-sided / PWID 5) CIED-related 6) Culture-negative … A) Ampicillin + (flu)cloxacillin + gentamicin; penicillin allergy: vancomycin + gentamicin — 4–6 weeks B) Vancomycin + gentamicin + rifampicin; ≥6 weeks; usually nosocomial staphylococci — assume MRSA; rifampicin added 3–5 days after starting the other two, once bacteraemia is clearing C) As for native valve, plus rifampicin if staphylococcal — ≥6 weeks D) Cover S. aureus — (flu)cloxacillin, or vancomycin/daptomycin if MRSA risk — 2 weeks may suffice for uncomplicated tricuspid MSSA IE E) As for staphylococcal IE — complete hardware extraction is mandatory; new device at a different site once cultures are clear F) Cover HACEK, Coxiella, Bartonella, Brucella, Tropheryma — serology + PCR
questions.exp: Book p71 table: Native valve community-acquired — ampicillin + (flu)cloxacillin + gentamicin (allergy: vancomycin + gentamicin), 4–6 weeks; Prosthetic EARLY — vancomycin + gentamicin + rifampicin, ≥6 weeks, assume MRSA, rifampicin 3–5 days later; Prosthetic LATE — as native + rifampicin if staphylococcal, ≥6 weeks; Right-sided/PWID — (flu)cloxacillin or vancomycin/daptomycin, 2 weeks may suffice for uncomplicated tricuspid MSSA; CIED — as staphylococcal IE, hardware extraction mandatory; Culture-negative — cover HACEK, Coxiella, Bartonella, Brucella, Tropheryma, serology + PCR. (Book p71)

questions.q: For streptococcal, fully sensitive native-valve IE (Book p71), penicillin or ceftriaxone runs for ____ weeks — or ____ weeks if combined with gentamicin.
questions.exp: Book p71: 'Streptococcal, fully sensitive: penicillin or ceftriaxone 4 weeks (2 weeks if combined with gentamicin)'. (Book p71)

questions.q: A patient 3 months after prosthetic aortic valve implantation presents with IE. Per the 2023 table (Book p71), the empirical regimen is:
opts: Vancomycin + gentamicin + rifampicin for ≥6 weeks — assume MRSA — with rifampicin added 3–5 days after starting the other two, once bacteraemia is clearing
questions.exp: Book p71 Prosthetic valve, EARLY (<12 months): Vancomycin + gentamicin + rifampicin; ≥6 weeks; usually nosocomial staphylococci — assume MRSA; rifampicin added 3–5 days after starting the other two, once bacteraemia is clearing. (Book p71)

questions.q: The right-sided / PWID row of the 2023 table (Book p71) states:
opts: A minimum of 6 weeks is mandatory for all right-sided IE
2 weeks may suffice for uncomplicated tricuspid MSSA IE, and septic pulmonary emboli must be looked for
Rifampicin is mandatory for all PWID IE
Hardware extraction is mandatory in PWID IE
questions.exp: Book p71: Right-sided / PWID — cover S. aureus ((flu)cloxacillin, or vancomycin/daptomycin if MRSA risk); '2 weeks may suffice for uncomplicated tricuspid MSSA IE. Look for septic pulmonary emboli'. (Book p71)

questions.q: In the culture-negative row of the 2023 table (Book p71), examiners should ask about prior ____, because that is the commonest cause of culture negativity.
questions.exp: Book p71 Culture-negative row: 'Serology + PCR. Ask about prior antibiotics — the commonest cause of culture negativity'. (Book p71)

questions.q: All of the following are on the culture-negative coverage list in the 2023 table (Book p71) EXCEPT:
questions.exp: Book p71 Culture-negative: 'Cover HACEK, Coxiella, Bartonella, Brucella, Tropheryma'. Nocardia is not on the list. (Book p71)

questions.q: Match the three H's of surgery indications on Book p71 to their detail — 1) Heart failure 2) Uncontrolled Infection 3) Prevention of Embolism … A) From valve destruction — the commonest and most urgent B) Abscess, false aneurysm, fistula, enlarging vegetation, persistent positive cultures >7 days, fungal or resistant organism C) Vegetation >10 mm with an embolic event, or >10 mm with severe valve stenosis/regurgitation, or isolated vegetation >15 mm
questions.exp: Book p71 'Surgery indications (the three H's)': Heart failure from valve destruction — the commonest and most urgent; uncontrolled Infection (abscess, false aneurysm, fistula, enlarging vegetation, persistent positive cultures >7 days, fungal or resistant organism); prevention of Embolism (vegetation >10 mm with an embolic event, or >10 mm with severe valve stenosis/regurgitation, or isolated vegetation >15 mm). (Book p71)

questions.q: Which of the following True/False statements correctly reflects the 2023 stroke-and-surgery guidance (Book p71)?
opts: True: after an ischaemic stroke without haemorrhage, surgery need not be delayed if otherwise indicated
False: after intracranial haemorrhage, surgery should be deferred about a month
True: stroke remains an automatic bar to surgery
False: heart failure from valve destruction is the commonest and most urgent surgery indication
questions.exp: Book p71: 'Stroke is no longer an automatic bar to surgery. After an ischaemic stroke without haemorrhage, surgery need not be delayed if otherwise indicated. After intracranial haemorrhage, defer about a month.' (Book p71)

questions.q: The POET trial on Book p71: in stabilised left-sided IE, switching to oral antibiotics to complete the course is ____; OPAT is endorsed for selected stable patients — not in the first ____ days, not in the presence of ____.
questions.exp: Book p71: 'Partial oral therapy (POET trial): in stabilised left-sided IE, switching to oral antibiotics to complete the course is non-inferior. OPAT is endorsed for selected stable patients — not in the first 10 days, not in the presence of complications.' (Book p71)

questions.q: The 2023 ESC recommendation on the Endocarditis Team and Heart Valve Centre (Book p71) states:
opts: Every case is discussed by cardiology, cardiac surgery, microbiology and imaging
Only prosthetic-valve cases require team discussion
Discussion is limited to cardiology and microbiology
Surgery is consulted only after a negative echocardiogram
questions.exp: Book p71: 'Endocarditis Team and Heart Valve Centre — a formal 2023 ESC recommendation. Every case discussed by cardiology, cardiac surgery, microbiology and imaging.' (Book p71)

questions.sec: 2023 Prophylaxis: The Principle (bottom of Book p71)
questions.q: The prophylaxis principle stated in section 3 at the foot of Book p71 is:
opts: Since 2007: prophylaxis for every cardiac lesion undergoing a dental procedure
Since 2007: prophylaxis is confined to high-risk patients undergoing high-risk procedures — moderate-risk cardiac lesions no longer qualify
New in 2023: moderate-risk lesions now qualify
Prophylaxis for all oral-mucosa procedures in every patient
questions.exp: Book p71, section 3 'PROPHYLAXIS — WHO, WHEN, WHAT': 'The principle since 2007 is unchanged: prophylaxis is confined to high-risk patients undergoing high-risk procedures. Moderate-risk cardiac lesions no longer qualify.' (Book p71)

questions.q: Match the four high-risk patient categories on Book p72 to their description — 1) Category 1 2) Category 2 3) Category 3 4) Category 4 … A) Prosthetic valve — surgical or transcatheter — or any prosthetic material used for valve repair B) Previous infective endocarditis C) Untreated cyanotic congenital heart disease, or CHD repaired with prosthetic material — for 6 months after the procedure, or lifelong if a residual shunt or regurgitation persists D) NEW in 2023 — recipients of a ventricular assist device or a heart transplant with valvulopathy
questions.exp: Book p72 WHICH PATIENTS (high risk only): 1. Prosthetic valve (surgical or transcatheter) or any prosthetic material used for valve repair; 2. Previous infective endocarditis; 3. Untreated cyanotic CHD, or CHD repaired with prosthetic material — 6 months after the procedure, or lifelong if a residual shunt or regurgitation persists; 4. NEW in 2023: recipients of a ventricular assist device or a heart transplant with valvulopathy. (Book p72)

questions.q: Match the 2023 prophylaxis procedure and regimen details on Book p72 — 1) WHICH PROCEDURES 2) NOT recommended 3) REGIMEN (single dose, 30–60 min before) 4) Penicillin-allergy regimen … A) Dental only — manipulation of the gingiva or the periapical region of the teeth, or perforation of the oral mucosa B) Respiratory, gastrointestinal, genitourinary, dermatological or musculoskeletal procedures in the absence of established infection — the point examiners test C) Amoxicillin or ampicillin 2 g PO/IV (children 50 mg/kg) D) Doxycycline 100 mg, or clindamycin 600 mg where still used; azithromycin/clarithromycin 500 mg are alternatives
questions.exp: Book p72: WHICH PROCEDURES — dental only (gingiva/periapical region or perforation of oral mucosa); NOT recommended for respiratory, GI, GU, dermatological or musculoskeletal procedures without established infection ('this is the point examiners test'); REGIMEN — amoxicillin or ampicillin 2 g PO/IV (children 50 mg/kg); penicillin allergy — doxycycline 100 mg, or clindamycin 600 mg where still used; azithromycin/clarithromycin 500 mg alternatives. (Book p72)

questions.q: Which of the following True/False statements correctly reflects the 2023 prophylaxis regimen (Book p72)?
opts: True: cephalosporins can be used safely in patients with anaphylaxis to penicillin
True: cephalosporins must not be used in patients with anaphylaxis to penicillin
False: doxycycline 100 mg is an alternative in penicillin allergy
False: amoxicillin or ampicillin 2 g PO/IV (children 50 mg/kg) is the single-dose regimen
questions.exp: Book p72: 'Cephalosporins must not be used in patients with anaphylaxis to penicillin'; the single dose is amoxicillin or ampicillin 2 g PO/IV (children 50 mg/kg), with doxycycline 100 mg or clindamycin 600 mg (where still used) and azithromycin/clarithromycin 500 mg as allergy alternatives. (Book p72)

questions.q: The 'ALWAYS, FOR EVERYONE' column on Book p72 states:
opts: Antibiotic prophylaxis matters more than oral hygiene

Good oral hygiene and regular dental review matter more than antibiotic prophylaxis — the cumulative bacteraemia of daily chewing and brushing far exceeds that of a single dental visit; aseptic technique for all vascular access and invasive procedures; discourage piercing and tattooing
Tattooing is safe for high-risk cardiac patients
Vascular access requires no special technique in IE patients
questions.exp: Book p72 ALWAYS, FOR EVERYONE: 'Good oral hygiene and regular dental review matter more than antibiotic prophylaxis — the cumulative bacteraemia of daily chewing and brushing far exceeds that of a single dental visit. Aseptic technique for all vascular access and invasive procedures. Discourage piercing and tattooing.' (Book p72)

questions.q: The single 2023 prophylaxis dose is given ____–60 minutes before the procedure, per Book p72.
questions.exp: Book p72 REGIMEN header: '(single dose, 30–60 min before)'. (Book p72)

questions.q: All of the following are 2023 HIGH-RISK patient categories for IE prophylaxis on Book p72 EXCEPT:
opts: A moderate-risk cardiac lesion without previous IE
questions.exp: Book p72 high-risk categories: prosthetic valve/material, previous IE, untreated cyanotic CHD (or prosthetic-repair CHD for 6 months/lifelong), and the 2023 addition of VAD/heart-transplant recipients with valvulopathy. Moderate-risk cardiac lesions no longer qualify (Book p71). (Book p72)

questions.q: For CHD repaired with prosthetic material (Book p72), prophylaxis lasts for ____ months after the procedure, or lifelong if a residual shunt or regurgitation persists.
questions.exp: Book p72 category 3: 'Untreated cyanotic congenital heart disease, or CHD repaired with prosthetic material — for 6 months after the procedure, or lifelong if a residual shunt or regurgitation persists'. (Book p72)

units.title: IE Diagnosis: Definite vs Possible (Book p69)
units.guide:
Definite: pathological criteria, 2 major + 1 minor, 1 major + 2 minor, or 5 minor.
Possible: 1 major + 1 minor, or 3 minor.

units.title: Duke Criteria: Major — Blood Cultures (Book p69)
units.guide:
Typical organisms from two cultures (Viridans streptococci, Streptococcus bovis, HACEK = Haemophilus, Actinobacillus, Cardiobacterium, Eikenella, Kingella), or community-acquired S. aureus/enterococci without a primary focus.
Other organisms from persistently positive cultures (two >12 h apart, or all of three/majority of four, first-last 1 h apart); single Coxiella burnetii culture or serology for Q fever, Bartonella, Chlamydia psittaci.

units.title: Duke Criteria: Major — Endocardial Involvement (Book p69)
units.guide:
Echocardiogram positive for IE: oscillating intracardiac mass without alternative explanation, abscess, or new partial dehiscence of prosthetic valve.
Or NEW valvular regurgitation — worsening/changing a preexisting murmur is not sufficient.

units.title: Duke Criteria: Minor & Pathological (Book p69)
units.guide:
Minors: predisposition (heart condition, injection drug use, previous IE, prosthetic material); fever >38°C; vascular phenomena (arterial emboli, septic pulmonary infarcts, mycotic aneurysm, intracranial haemorrhages, subconjunctival petechiae, Janeway lesions); immunologic (glomerulonephritis, Osler's nodes, Roth's spots, positive rheumatoid factor); microbiological evidence.
Pathological: positive microbiology or histology of pathologic tissue at surgery or autopsy (vegetations, valve tissue, embolic fragments, tissue/pus from intracardiac abscesses).

units.title: IE Prophylaxis — Old Regimens (Book p70, superseded)
units.guide:
Oral procedures: can take oral — amoxicillin; cannot take oral — ampicillin; ceftriaxone; allergy row — clindamycin; azithro (oral) / clindamycin; ceftriaxone (IV). RESP: same as oral; abscess/empyema drainage add strep viridans; staph — Vanco.
GU/GIT: not recommended (established infx/abx cover — enterococci: penicillin); SSTI: not for routine sx (infected tissue — penicillin; allergic or MRSA — Vance). The 2023 ESC + Duke-ISCVID pages supersede all of this, including prophylaxis.

units.title: 2023 Update: What Duke-ISCVID Changed (Book p71)
units.guide:
Definite IE unchanged (2 major / 1 major + 3 minor / 5 minor); possible 1 major + 1 minor or 3 minor. Blood-culture rules relaxed; second organism tier (coagulase-negative staphylococci, Cutibacterium acnes, corynebacteria — typical only with intracardiac prosthetic material).
New microbiology (PCR, amplicon/metagenomic sequencing, in-situ hybridisation, Bartonella enzyme immunoassay); cardiac CT + 18F-FDG PET/CT major (no longer prosthetic-only); intraoperative inspection a new major; previous IE + transcatheter valves/CIEDs as new minors.

units.title: 2023 Update: Management by Type (Book p71)
units.guide:
Native community-acquired: ampicillin + (flu)cloxacillin + gentamicin (allergy: vancomycin + gentamicin), 4–6 weeks; streptococcal fully sensitive: penicillin/ceftriaxone 4 weeks (2 weeks with gentamicin).
Prosthetic EARLY: vancomycin + gentamicin + rifampicin ≥6 weeks (assume MRSA; rifampicin 3–5 days later); LATE: as native + rifampicin if staph; right-sided/PWID: 2 weeks may suffice for uncomplicated tricuspid MSSA, look for septic pulmonary emboli; CIED: hardware extraction mandatory; culture-negative: HACEK, Coxiella, Bartonella, Brucella, Tropheryma (prior antibiotics = commonest cause).

units.title: 2023 Update: Team, Surgery, Stroke, POET (Book p71)
units.guide:
Endocarditis Team and Heart Valve Centre: every case discussed by cardiology, cardiac surgery, microbiology and imaging.
Surgery (three H's): heart failure (commonest/most urgent), uncontrolled infection (abscess, false aneurysm, fistula, enlarging vegetation, cultures >7 days, fungal/resistant), embolism prevention (>10 mm with embolus or severe valve disease, or isolated >15 mm). Stroke no longer an automatic bar (ischaemic without haemorrhage: no delay; ICH: defer ~1 month). POET: oral switch non-inferior in stabilised left-sided IE; OPAT not in the first 10 days, not with complications.

units.title: 2023 Prophylaxis: The Principle (bottom of Book p71)
units.sec: 2023 Prophylaxis: The Principle (bottom of Book p71)
units.guide:
The principle since 2007 is unchanged: prophylaxis is confined to high-risk patients undergoing high-risk procedures.
Moderate-risk cardiac lesions no longer qualify.

units.title: 2023 Prophylaxis: Who, When, What (Book p72)
units.guide:
Who (high risk only): prosthetic valve/material; previous IE; untreated cyanotic CHD or prosthetic-repair CHD (6 months, or lifelong with residual shunt/regurgitation); NEW 2023 — VAD or heart-transplant recipients with valvulopathy.
When: dental only (gingiva/periapical manipulation or oral-mucosa perforation) — NOT respiratory/GI/GU/dermatological/musculoskeletal without established infection. What: amoxicillin or ampicillin 2 g PO/IV single dose 30–60 min before (children 50 mg/kg); allergy — doxycycline 100 mg, clindamycin 600 mg, azithro/clarithro 500 mg; no cephalosporins with penicillin anaphylaxis. Oral hygiene and dental review outweigh prophylaxis; aseptic technique; discourage piercing/tattooing.
